 Shreveport Times New Orleans congressman casts historic vote for speaker
 Greg Hilburn, Shreveport Times Updated Wed, November 18, 2026 at 6:06 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Louisiana Democratic Congressman Troy Carter cast a historic vote for Hakeem Jeffries of New York to become the first Black speaker of the House in history when the new Congress convenes Jan. 3.
 "The Democratic Caucus has spoken," the New Orleans congressman said in a post on X after the Democrats voted Nov. 18. "My friend, colleague, and Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity Inc. brother Hakeem Jeffries is officially our nominee for Speaker. When elected, he'll make history as the first African American Speaker of the U.S. House. I'm proud to stand with you, Brother Jeffries, Mr. Speaker!!
 "We run to win, we win to Govern"!
 House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) holds a news conference at the U.S. Capitol on Nov. 9, 2026 in Washington, DC. Jeffries spoke on the Democrats' new majority following the midterm elections and outlined the party's agenda. Jeffries won't officially become the next speaker until the full House votes Jan. 3. He will take over from Shreveport's Mike Johnson, who led the House for three years before the Democrats won the majority in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Democrats voted 251-11 in favor of Jeffries in the intraparty election.
 In an interview with USA Today Network, Carter expressed confidence in Jeffries' leadership.
 "He has the ability to lead and be strategic, smart and cohesive, all of the things required to advance an agenda important to the American people," Carter said.
 Troy Carter's congressional clout: Will Louisiana Democrat Troy Carter support impeaching President Trump? 
 Carter's congressional clout is also on the rise as Democrats take control of the next Congress, where Carter is expected to lead the largest Congressional Black Caucus in history.
 Advertisement Advertisement The vote for chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus is scheduled Dec. 2.
 Greg Hilburn covers state politics for the USA TODAY Network of Louisiana. Follow him on Twitter @GregHilburn1.
